title: Accelerated finite-field projections and pointwise finite cochain differences
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended nonarchimedean norm [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and its isometric inclusion in the norm completion $B=\widehat\Omega$ [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Let $(F_N)_{N\geq0}$ be increasing intermediate fields, finite-dimensional over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with union $\Omega$. Let $S$ be a nonempty profinite space and $G$ a profinite group, meaning compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces, with continuous group operations on $G$. For a coefficient space $V$ let $C_V^r=C(S\times G^r,V)$, with trivial action and
$$(dh)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=h(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^a h(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}h(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r),$$
where $C_V^0=C(S,V)$ and $d^0=0$. Fix $n\geq2$, $z\in C_\Omega^n$ with $dz=0$, and $b\in C_B^{n-1}$ with $db=z$ in $B$. Given any integers $N_j\geq0$ and real constants $C_j\geq1$, $j\geq1$, set $D_t=\max(1,C_1,\ldots,C_t)$ and $\delta_i=2^{-i}/D_{i+1}$ for $i\geq0$. There exist continuous $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear contractions $Q_N:B\to F_N$ fixing $F_N$, and strictly increasing integers $L_i\geq i$ with $L_i\geq N_j$ for $1\leq j\leq i+1$, such that, writing $P_i=Q_{L_i}$ and $P_{-1}=0$,
$$\|P_i z-z\|_\infty\leq\delta_i,\qquad \|P_i b-b\|_\infty\leq\delta_i.$$
Here maps into finite fields are also viewed in $\Omega$ or $B$ by inclusion and $\|h\|_\infty=\sup_x|h(x)|$. The continuous cochains
$$e_i=(P_i-P_{i-1})z\in C_{F_{L_i}}^n,\qquad c_i=(P_i-P_{i-1})b\in C_{F_{L_i}}^{n-1}$$
satisfy $de_i=0$, $dc_i=e_i$ and $\sum_{h=0}^ie_h=P_i z\to z$ uniformly. For $i\geq1$ both norms are at most $\max(\delta_i,\delta_{i-1})$, and hence at most $2^{-(i-1)}/D_i$. For each fixed $(s,y)\in S\times G^n$, $e_i(s,y)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. If $j\leq i$ and the homogeneous function $f_z(s;-)$ takes values in $F_{N_j}$ on any subset $R\subseteq G^{n+1}$, then $f_{e_i}(s;-)$ is zero on $R$, where $f_h(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)=h(s;g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$. No pointwise eventual vanishing is asserted for $c_i$, and no retraction $B\to\Omega$ is assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: For each $N$, apply [lem-sfb-norm-one-finite-subfield-projection] to $F_N\subseteq\Omega$, obtaining an $F_N$-linear contraction $p_N:\Omega\to F_N$ fixing $F_N$. It is in particular $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear. The restricted absolute value on $F_N$ extends the given one on $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $F_N$ is finite-dimensional, so [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] makes $F_N$ complete. By definition the completion embedding has dense image; identify $\Omega$ with that linear subspace of $B$ using [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Multiplicativity of the completion norm gives $|av|=|a||v|$ for $a\in\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $v\in B$; its restriction does the same on $F_N$. Thus both are normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector spaces, with the stated norm topologies. Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] with $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$, ambient space $B$, dense subspace $\Omega$, target $F_N$, and map $p_N$. Obtain a continuous $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear contraction $Q_N:B\to F_N$, agreeing with $p_N$ and hence fixing $F_N$. Choose one for each $N$. The norm on $B$ is ultrametric: for $x,y\in B$ choose sequences from $\Omega$ tending to them and pass to the limit in $|x_m+y_m|\leq\max(|x_m|,|y_m|)$, using the ordinary norm continuity inequality $\big||u|-|v|\big|\leq|u-v|$.

proof.text:
The domains $X_r=S\times G^r$ are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] applied to their finite families of compact factors (Stacks Tag 08ZU, theorem-tychonov). For $h=z$ or $h=b$ viewed in $B$ and any $\epsilon>0$, the sets $h^{-1}(\{v:|v-a|<\epsilon\})$, $a\in\Omega$, form an open cover of its domain: density supplies an $a$ near each $h(x)$. Take a finite subcover. All its centers lie in some common $F_M$, since the fields increase and cover $\Omega$. For $N\geq M$ and a center $a$ with $|h(x)-a|<\epsilon$, linearity, contractivity and $Q_N(a)=a$ give
$$|Q_Nh(x)-h(x)|=|Q_N(h(x)-a)-(h(x)-a)|\leq|h(x)-a|<\epsilon.$$
Thus $\|Q_Nh-h\|_\infty\leq\epsilon$ for every $N\geq M$. Taking the larger of the two indices works for $z$ and $b$ simultaneously. The suprema are finite: the same finite cover with $\epsilon=1$ bounds $|h(x)|$ by $\max(1,\max_a|a|)$, and $|Q_Nh(x)|\leq|h(x)|$.

proof.text:
Each $D_t$ is a finite real number at least $1$, so each $\delta_i>0$. Step 2 with $\epsilon=\delta_i$ gives $M_i$ such that both errors are at most $\delta_i$ for every $N\geq M_i$. Choose recursively $L_0\geq\max(M_0,N_1,0)$ and
$$L_i\geq\max(M_i,L_{i-1}+1,i,N_1,\ldots,N_{i+1})\quad(i\geq1).$$
Then $L_i$ strictly increases, $L_i\geq i$, all required $N_j$ are dominated, and $P_i=Q_{L_i}$ has the two required error bounds. This is only a choice above a finite list of integers at each stage.

proof.text: Put $T_i=P_i-P_{i-1}$ with $P_{-1}=0$. For $i\geq1$, both summands have values in $F_{L_i}$ because $F_{L_{i-1}}\subseteq F_{L_i}$; the same holds for $i=0$. Subtraction and composition preserve continuity, so $e_i=T_i z$ and $c_i=T_i b$ are continuous cochains with the stated coefficient fields and degrees. Every term in the displayed differential is a value of the cochain with coefficient $+1$ or $-1$. Consequently $d(Th)=T(dh)$ for each $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear coefficient map $T$, by applying its additivity term by term to that finite displayed sum. Hence $de_i=T_i(dz)=0$ and $dc_i=T_i(db)=T_i z=e_i$ as equalities in $B$, and thus in $F_{L_i}$ by the injective field inclusions. This uses no assertion about general group cohomology or $d^2$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar analytic expansion: continuous telescoping differences and coefficientwise differential identities

proof.text:
For either $h=z$ or $h=b$ and $i\geq1$, write
$$T_i h=(P_i h-h)-(P_{i-1}h-h).$$
The ultrametric inequality gives $\|T_i h\|_\infty\leq\max(\delta_i,\delta_{i-1})$. Since $D_{i+1}\geq D_i\geq1$,
$$\delta_i=2^{-i}/D_{i+1}\leq 2^{-(i-1)}/D_i=\delta_{i-1}.$$
This proves both requested estimates. Finite telescoping gives $\sum_{h=0}^i e_h=P_i z$. Finally $\delta_i\leq2^{-i}\to0$, so the error bound gives uniform convergence to $z$ in its original norm topology as well as in $B$, since the inclusion is isometric. No infinite summation in $\Omega$ is needed for this convergence statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar analytic expansion: ultrametric error estimates and uniform convergence of finite telescoping sums

proof.text: Fix $(s,y)\in S\times G^n$. There is $M$ with $z(s,y)\in F_M$. If $i\geq M+1$, then $L_{i-1}\geq i-1\geq M$ and $L_i\geq M$, so both $P_i$ and $P_{i-1}$ fix $z(s,y)$. Their difference is zero there. For the last clause fix $j\geq1$ and $i\geq j$. The index bounds imply $L_{i-1}\geq N_j$ (since $j\leq(i-1)+1$) and $L_i\geq N_j$. For any $(g_0,\ldots,g_n)\in R$, the value $f_z(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)$ lies in $F_{N_j}$, so both projections fix it. Substituting the definition of $f_h$ yields $f_{e_i}=P_i f_z-P_{i-1}f_z=0$ on $R$. This reasoning allows $R$ to be arbitrary and does not use its topology. It does not apply to a value of $b$ outside $\Omega$, and no eventual vanishing of $c_i$ follows or is needed.
